note: The interaction vocabulary (CORE-SPEC §2). Ten verbs, closed. Packs cannot define new ones — a pack that wants one is a core change request — because a finite verb list is what keeps the animation state machine and the netcode's action encoding finite. The names live in code (`VerbSet.VOCABULARY`) and this file supplies each one's detail, for the same reason `SlotSet.KINDS` is in code: a data file that could add a verb would imply packs may, and they may not.
status: First cut, written at C4 when the verb system became real. `dig` is live; the rest are declared and reserved to a named milestone, the way ANIMATION-SPEC handles its 24 states. A verb reserved to a milestone is a promise with an owner; a verb nobody has thought about is a gap, and the difference should be visible here rather than in someone's memory. **The status of a verb flips in the same diff that builds it, never ahead of it** — a file claiming a verb works when nothing dispatches it is the exact drift this field exists to catch.
slot_note: `slots` lists the archetype slots that can dispatch this verb. A slot may appear under more than one verb, and that is not a modelling failure: an entrenching tool is `melee_light` and it both digs a hole and hits people, which is exactly why it was issued. What a slot may NOT do is name a verb that is not in the vocabulary.

fire.what: Loose a projectile from a readied weapon, at a cost in ammunition and time.
fire.note: C4's done-condition is this verb: a weapon defined in data fires, and a bow and a rifle are the same code path. Both of those live in `ranged_slow`, whose own note has said `bolt rifle, musket, crossbow, bow` since C1. Reserved rather than live until dispatch carries it out: C4's own increment, and the status flips in the diff that builds it rather than ahead of it.

throw.what: Send an object on a ballistic arc from the hand rather than from a barrel.
throw.note: The flight is C4 and is the same ballistics as `fire` with a different launch. What it does when it lands is C5's blast model — the same split already drawn at C3, where `EarthCrater` is the earth's half of an explosion and not the explosion. A grenade in C4 flies, bounces and goes quiet. Reserved until `fire`'s ballistics exist, since the flight is the same maths with a different launch.

dig.what: Cut earth out of the ground and pile it where it can be stood behind.
dig.note: Calls straight into C3's field — carve, deposit, the settle queue and the event log — and is here mainly because it proves the verb table is not weapon-shaped. A vocabulary whose only live members shot things would not have been tested for the thing it is for.

melee.what: Strike at reach, resolved without a projectile.
melee.note: C4's, alongside ballistics, because CORE-SPEC puts melee resolution in the combat module — and because it is the cheapest proof that damage is not a property of projectiles. Blocking, stamina and directional defence are not in scope: the slots list them optional and nothing supplies them yet. Reserved until damage resolution exists for it to call.

build.what: Place a buildable, paying its cost, where the ground and the neighbours allow it.
build.note: Reserved rather than built, and the reason is a judgement call recorded in `DEVIATIONS-C4.md`: placing a sandbag wall is easy, and a sandbag wall that does not yet topple sideways where a clay one slumps is a prop rather than a buildable. C5 switches material behaviour on, and that is when placing one means something.

carry.what: Bear an object or a burden, at a cost in movement.
carry.note: The loadout system in C4 decides what a soldier is holding. Carrying is the other thing — an ammunition crate walked forward from a dump — and it has no purpose until C7 builds the supply chain that makes the walk worth making. No slot dispatches it; the thing carried is cargo, not kit.

enter.what: Take a seat in a vehicle or a mount, and leave it again.
enter.note: C6 owns multi-crew seats and enter/exit animation by name. Declared now so the vocabulary is closed at C4 rather than growing later, which is the whole claim.

man.what: Take a crew station on something that is not going anywhere.
man.note: Distinct from `enter` because a crew station is a role rather than a ride: two soldiers on one gun are loader and layer, and C6's hands-on-controls IK is what makes the distinction visible. The gun slots appear under `fire` too — manning it and firing it are different verbs on the same object.

interact.what: Use a thing whose whole purpose is being used — a lever, a flag, a field telephone.
interact.note: The catch-all, and the one to watch: a verb that means anything means nothing, and the first time a pack wants `interact` to do something specific is the moment to ask whether it wanted a real verb instead. C7's capture and phase logic is its first real customer.

signal.what: Tell other people something without a menu — point, whistle, wave, fire a flare.
signal.note: Reserved to C7 with the AI behaviour set, because a signal nobody can receive is an animation. Listed here rather than treated as UI: it is a thing a soldier's body does in the world, it costs time, and it can be seen by the other side.
